claims.text: The relative contributions of Nb and Ti govern superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloy superconductors by modulating the effective density of states at the Fermi level and electron–phonon coupling.
Increasing Ti relative to Ta enhances electron–phonon coupling despite compositional disorder.
Increasing Ti relative to Ta raises both the superconducting transition temperature and the upper critical field.
The relevant initial material is a homogeneous multicomponent transition-metal high-entropy alloy.
The relevant initial material has a body-centered-cubic structure.
HEAs of interest contain constituents in the approximate range of 5–35 atomic percent.
The relevant superconducting transition-temperature regime is approximately 4–10 K.
A representative upper critical field for the baseline alloy is approximately 12 T.
HEA superconductors in the (TaNb)-(ZrHfTi) family can be single-band isotropic s-wave superconductors in the dirty limit.
The crystalline lattice has a random elemental distribution.
Local chemical fluctuations in the random lattice modulate the electronic density of states.
Substitution of Ti for Ta increases the density of states.
The studied Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 alloy has an intermediate electron–phonon coupling strength.
Compositional disorder does not suppress pairing because enhanced density of states and electron–phonon coupling compensate for it.
Higher-Ti, lower-Ta alloys should have higher transition temperatures and upper critical fields than otherwise similar Nb-Ta-containing HEAs.
Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 is an experimentally studied HEA superconductor suitable as the proposed baseline.
The proposed baseline alloy has a superconducting transition temperature near 7.5 K and an upper critical field of 12.2 T.
The boundary condition assumes electron–phonon-mediated, isotropic s-wave BCS superconductivity in the dirty limit.
Observed transition-temperature variations between compositionally different films in this HEA family cannot be explained by disorder effects alone.
